emma_sales: Quick sync — FinServe (Brazil + EU) pushed back on a couple of items for the POC: they need strict EU-only residency for EU tenants even during failover, plus a list of sub-processors for Sao Paulo and any certs. Also want a rough Delta between Hosted+tenant_pin vs Dedicated pricing for 100/500 RPS.
raj_se: Quick overview: we support regional pinning (tenant_pin) and routing policies. If tenant_pin=true then traffic stays in the pinned region and we won't failover across legal boundaries. If tenant_pin=false, automatic failover can go to nearest healthy region which may cross borders.
oliver_infra: For LATAM we run in GCP sa-east1 (São Paulo) and also have multi-tenant presence in us-south/sa-east. We don’t currently have a separate BR-only Dedicated zone. Subprocessors in sa-east1: GCP (sa-east1), Logshifter (log vendor, data-at-rest in sa-east1), CloudMetrics (monitoring).
marta_legal: We can provide DPA + standard SCCs for transfers. For LGPD-specific wording we can add a clause mirroring SCC obligations and limit cross-border transfers except per the routing policy. Need to confirm whether they require audit of our GCP subprocessor in Brazil.
nana_customer: @emma_sales thanks. They insisted: "EU data must never leave EU for processing or caching except with explicit legal/process exceptions (e.g., court order)." They also asked if support engineers ever access EU data from non-EU IPs.
raj_se: Important nuance: tenant_pin + region_fallback_only will keep compute and KV cache in EU and only allow failover to other EU regions. If no EU spare region is available, behavior options are: return 503 / degrade features / failover to Dedicated in another EU region. We can enforce return-503-on-failover to satisfy legal requirement. :eyes:
raj_se: Sample routing policy snippet for POC:
```
routing_policy:
  region_preference: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]
  failover_mode: "region_fallback_only"   # only fallback to other EU regions
  tenant_pin: true                          # pin tenant data + cache to preferred region
  on_no_eu_capacity: "reject"             # options: reject | degrade | allow_cross_region
```
emma_sales: Can you also share a curl example to pin the tenant for the POC? I'll send to the customer.
raj_se: Sure: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"tenant_id":"finserve-eu","region_pin":"eu-west-1","routing_policy": {"failover_mode":"region_fallback_only","on_no_eu_capacity":"reject"}}'
```
oliver_infra: Pricing context: Hosted with tenant_pin is functionally same as hosted for token billing; however availability SLAs change (we reserve capacity for pinned tenants during POC windows on request). Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing ballpark: ~ $22k/month for 100 RPS baseline with committed GPUs and support; ~ $85k/month for 500 RPS depending on model family and quantization. These are rough — sales to produce formal quote.
marta_legal: On support access: we can restrict engineer access to EU-only IPs via our access controls for the customer’s tenants and log all access. For emergency cross-border access we have an escalation process with documented approvals. We'll add that language to the DPA addendum.
nana_customer: They want the subprocessor list and SOC2 certs for each vendor in Brazil. Also asked about whether KV cache shards ever replicate outside region.
raj_se: KV cache is region-local when tenant_pin=true. We do asynchronous backups to our control plane for metadata; backups can be configured to stay in-region for Private deployments. For hosted POC we can set backup retention to EU-only. I'll attach a short note on cache semantics.
raj_se: Attach (pasted): "Cache semantics: primary KV cache is local to serving region. Replication to other regions only occurs if tenant_pin=false or during explicit DR ops which require 'on_no_eu_capacity: allow_cross_region' setting. Backups can be configured to be EU-only or customer-managed in Private." 
emma_sales: Next steps: 1) I'll send the subprocessor CSV + SOC2 links to the customer (marta, pls review) 2) raj, pls confirm the routing snippet is valid for our hosted POC infra and include expected behavior when eu regions saturated 3) oliver, pls prepare rough dedicated quote for 100 & 500 RPS incl. reservation options and support tier.
marta_legal: I'll review subproc list and draft the LGPD paragraph. Can also request vendor evidence for Logshifter if customer insists.
oliver_infra: I'll spin up a POC org and tag it `redwood-poc-finserve-1918000000`. deploy-bot will post when ready.
deploy-bot: POC org created: redwood-poc-finserve-1918000000. Endpoint: https://eu.api.redwood.ai/poc/finserve-eu. POC creds sent to sec-vault. :white_check_mark:
nana_customer: Great, thanks everyone. Expecting the subproc list + DPA language today.
emma_sales: Will do. tagging timeline: subproc/SOC2 + DPA draft by EOD, routing confirmation + cache note by @raj_se within 4 hours, Dedicated quote by @oliver_infra EOD. :thumbsup:
raj_se: On it, will test the `on_no_eu_capacity: reject` behavior in the staging cluster and report back.
oliver_infra: ETA for Dedicated sketch: EOD PST.
marta_legal: Will loop in privacy counsel if vendor evidence is requested.
(End of thread)
